changes.sourceChinese: 少孤，兄弟皆早亡，單煢獨立，雖宗族無能識者，惟叔父耽幼而奇之，曰：「此兒非惟吾門之標秀，乃佐時之良器也。」
changes.before: Orphaned young, with brothers dead early, he stood alone; few in the clan knew him, but his uncle Dan marveled at him even in youth and said, "This child is not only our clan's outstanding ornament but an instrument to serve the age."
changes.after: Orphaned young, with all his brothers also dying early, he stood utterly alone. None even in his clan recognized his worth; only his uncle Dan thought him extraordinary while he was still young, saying, "This child is not only an outstanding talent of our family but also a fine instrument for serving the age."
changes.reason: 雖宗族無能識者 means none of the clan recognized his worth, not merely that few knew him; 幼 refers to Yu when Dan recognized his promise.

changes.sourceChinese: 裕謂友人成泮曰：「仲尼喜佛肸之召，以匏瓜自喻，伊尹亦稱何事非君，何使非民，聖賢尚如此，況吾曹乎！
changes.before: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius rejoiced at Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a gourd; Yi Yin too said, 'What affair is not that of the lord? What people are not his subjects?' Even sages were thus, how much more we!
changes.after: Yang Yu told his friend Cheng Pan, "Confucius welcomed Bi Xi's summons and likened himself to a bottle gourd; Yi Yin also said, 'Whom may I not serve as ruler? Whose people may I not serve?' If even sages and worthies acted thus, how much more should we!
changes.reason: 何事非君，何使非民 concerns serving a ruler and a people, not asking which affairs or people belong to a lord. The whole speech segment is replaced without pretending to supply the next unit.

changes.sourceChinese: 卿追蹤伊、孔，抑亦知機其神也。」
changes.before: You follow Confucius and Yi Yin—you know when Heaven calls.”
changes.after: You follow in the footsteps of Yi Yin and Confucius; surely your insight into the first signs of change is also extraordinary.”
changes.reason: 知機其神 concerns discerning incipient opportunities or changes; Heaven calling is not in this Chinese unit. This repeated Yi/Confucius use is reviewed independently of s0193.

changes.sourceChinese: 及遷都和龍，裕雅有巧思，皝所制城池宮闔，皆裕之規模。
changes.before: When the capital shifted to Helong, Yang Yu’s engineering shaped every wall and tower Murong Huang built.
changes.after: When the capital was moved to Helong, Yang Yu, who had long possessed an ingenious mind, drew up the plans for all the city walls, moats, palaces and gates that Murong Huang built.
changes.reason: 城池宮闔 includes moats and the palace/gate complex; wall and tower alone omits these objects and does not express 皆裕之規模 as Yu’s plans.

changes.sourceChinese: 裕雖仕皝日近，寵秩在舊人之右，性謙恭清儉，剛簡慈篤，雖曆居朝端，若布衣之士。
changes.before: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
changes.after: Although Yang Yu had served Murong Huang for only a short time, his favor and rank surpassed those of the old retainers. By nature he was humble, respectful, upright and frugal, firm and straightforward, compassionate and sincere; although he successively held leading posts at court, he lived like a scholar in plain clothes.
changes.reason: 仕皝日近 means his service under Huang was recent or short, not that he grew daily closer to Huang. The complete unit retains the contrast in rank and his personal qualities.

changes.sourceChinese: 士大夫流亡羈絕者，莫不經營收葬，存恤孤遺，士無賢不肖皆傾身待之，是以所在推仰。
changes.before: He buried exiles, aided their orphans, and honored every gentleman he met, winning universal esteem.
changes.after: For displaced and isolated gentlemen who died, he invariably arranged their collection and burial, cared for the orphans and bereaved they left, and devoted himself to receiving gentlemen, worthy or unworthy alike; thus he was esteemed wherever he went.
changes.reason: 經營收葬 and 存恤孤遺 distinguish burial arrangements from care for survivors; 士無賢不肖皆傾身待之 explicitly includes worthy and unworthy, a distinction omitted by the current English.
